title: Boolean Logic
definition: Boolean logic combines true and false propositions through formally defined logical operations.
purpose: Model decisions as explicit, testable truth relationships.
history: Boolean algebra formalized two-valued symbolic reasoning and became foundational to digital circuits and programming decisions.
mental_model: Each proposition is a question with true or false as its answer; logical operations combine those answers according to fixed tables.
analogy: A set of labeled switches can model true and false inputs; the analogy fails when programming-language operators return operand values or skip evaluation.
common_mistakes: Confusing natural-language and/or with formal semantics
Mixing Boolean values and truthy values
industry_notes: Complex decision logic should expose named predicates, complete cases, and readable grouping.
ai_notes: AI-generated conditions must be checked with truth tables and counterexamples rather than accepted from plausible prose.
interview_notes: Ask the candidate to build and explain a truth table for a compound rule.
lab_candidates: Model access rules with truth tables
